sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world.

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，在这里，我们当然要剖析一下二十岁时的心理状态。

sentences.en: Let's be so real right now.
sentences.zh: 咱们现在就开诚布公地说吧。

sentences.en: Saying what we mean and what we feel is really hard, and it is certainly not helped by some of the sensations we feel afterwards.
sentences.zh: 表达我们的真实想法和感受其实非常困难，而且事后产生的某些情绪体验也绝对帮不上什么忙。

sentences.en: The kind of cringiness of feeling like we overshared, that we said too much to the wrong person.
sentences.zh: 那种觉得自己分享过头、对不该说的人说了太多话的尴尬感，实在让人脚趾抠地。

sentences.en: In other words, the experience of a vulnerability hangover.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这就是一种“敞开心扉后的情绪宿醉”体验。

sentences.en: It's something you and I, the whole world, every person has most likely experienced at some stage.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是你、我、全世界、甚至每个人在某个阶段都极有可能经历过的事情。

sentences.en: You know, you confess your romantic feelings for someone, you say the wrong thing after a night of drinking, you share too much,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，比如你向某人倾诉了浪漫的情愫，在喝完酒后说错了话，或者分享了太多隐私，

sentences.en: and afterwards, it just feels like the world is going to end.
sentences.zh: 然后事后就会觉得世界仿佛都要毁灭了。

sentences.en: But vulnerability hangovers are actually remarkably and entirely normal.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，情绪宿醉是非常罕见且完全正常的现象。

sentences.en: They occur for so many reasons.
sentences.zh: 它的出现有诸多原因。

sentences.en: The biggest one being that, in general, when we are seriously open and honest, so many times we bring things to the surface that usually we are not exposed to on the day-to-day.
sentences.zh: 其中最主要的原因是，通常当我们做到绝对的坦诚和真诚时，很多时候我们会把一些平时日常生活中不会轻易触及的东西翻到表面上来。

sentences.en: And that creates a major flood, a high, a breach in our walls, and then the next day, we crash.
sentences.zh: 这就造成了一场大洪水、一种极度亢奋、冲破了我们的心理防线，然后到了第二天，我们就彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: You feel everything at once when you're vulnerable with other people, either accidentally or on purpose, and then you have to get back to your equilibrium.
sentences.zh: 当你向他人敞开心扉时——无论是无意还是故意——你会同时感受到所有的情绪，然后你不得不努力恢复内心平衡。

sentences.en: Your mind and, to an extent, your body, they're just trying to adjust, and that's why this sense of being emotionally hungover occurs.
sentences.zh: 你的大脑，甚至在某种程度上还有你的身体，都只是在试图去适应这种状态，这就是为什么会出现这种情绪宿醉感的原因。

sentences.en: It certainly doesn't help that there is an implicit stigma around oversharing.
sentences.zh: 而社会对“分享过度”普遍存在一种无形的污名化，这绝对是火上浇油。

sentences.en: There is shame directed towards big emotions,
sentences.zh: 人们往往会对强烈的情感抱有羞耻感，

sentences.en: and that at times, you know, people are going to betray our trust and let us down.
sentences.zh: 并且有时，你懂的，人们会背叛我们的信任并让我们失望。

sentences.en: And so, time and time again, we often learn to associate vulnerability with its downsides and its consequences rather than many of its implicit benefits.
sentences.zh: 因此，一次又一次地，我们常常学会将敞开心扉与它的负面影响和后果联系起来，而不是去看到它带来的诸多潜在好处。

sentences.en: But today, my lovely listeners, we are going to break down, really break down, what is going on in your body, in your mind, in the social and emotional centers of your brain
sentences.zh: 但今天，我可爱的听众们，我们要剖析，真正深入地剖析，当你在敞开心扉以及在事情发生之后，

sentences.en: when you are vulnerable and in the aftermath.
sentences.zh: 你的身体里、你的头脑中、以及你大脑中负责社交和情感的中心到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: And why so many of the current scientific findings are saying that our lack of everyday vulnerability and the aversion and negative reactions we have to vulnerability
sentences.zh: 以及为什么许多最新的科学研究表明，我们日常生活中缺乏敞开心扉的勇气，以及我们对坦诚相待的抗拒和消极反应，

sentences.en: is what is causing rising levels of loneliness, disconnection, mistrust, and division.
sentences.zh: 正是导致孤独感、疏离感、不信任感和分裂感不断加剧的罪魁祸首。

sentences.en: You know, it's this episode, when I started writing it, when I started thinking about it, I was like, oh, it's this one thing,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当开始撰写这一期节目、开始思考这个主题时，我当时就在想，哦，就是这么一回事儿，

sentences.en: and it actually turned into this whole other discussion around what we need as humans, what we aren't getting as humans, and how that is actually kind of hurting society.
sentences.zh: 但它实际上演变成了一场全新的讨论，探讨作为人类我们真正需要什么、我们作为人类未能得到什么，以及这实际上是如何在某种程度上伤害了整个社会的。

sentences.en: All of it coming back to this one idea of vulnerability hangovers, which kind of seem rather inconspicuous, but here we go.
sentences.zh: 这一切都归结为一个概念，那就是情绪宿醉，它看起来似乎相当不起眼，但我们这就开始吧。

sentences.en: There is so much to cover, so much to get into.
sentences.zh: 有太多内容需要涵盖，有太多细节需要深入探讨了。

sentences.en: We're also going to talk about what you can do if you are currently experiencing a vulnerability or an oversharing hangover, and just so much more.
sentences.zh: 我们还将讨论如果你目前正在经历情绪或分享过度的宿醉，你可以做些什么，以及更多精彩内容。

sentences.en: So let's get into it.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们切入正题吧。

sentences.en: Let's start with a basic history lesson and a basic definition before we get into some of the nuances of this emotional experience.
sentences.zh: 在我们探讨这种情感体验的一些细微差别之前，让我们先从一个基础的历史小常识和一个基本定义开始。

sentences.en: The term vulnerability hangover comes from none other than the brilliant author and academic
sentences.zh: “情绪宿醉”这个词出自杰出的作家兼学者——

sentences.en: Brene Brown, who we know and love for her books.
sentences.zh: 布琳·布朗（Brene Brown），她的书籍我们都非常熟悉且喜爱。

sentences.en: What's her big one?
sentences.zh: 她最棒的作品是什么？

sentences.en: Dare to Lead.
sentences.zh: 《极地勇敢》（Dare to Lead）。

sentences.en: I also love her book,
sentences.zh: 我也很喜欢她的书，

sentences.en: The Gift of Imperfection.
sentences.zh: 《不完美的力量》（The Gift of Imperfection）。

sentences.en: She also did an incredible TED Talk called The Power of Vulnerability, where she essentially lays down this core platform or idea that what gives life meaning is connection,
sentences.zh: 她还做过一场精彩绝伦的 TED 演讲，名为《脆弱的力量》，她在演讲中基本上奠定了这个核心平台或观点：赋予生命意义的是连接，

sentences.en: and what creates connection is vulnerability.
sentences.zh: 而创造连接的则是敞开心扉的脆弱性。

sentences.en: And if you take all that reasoning back to its origin, essentially what she's saying is vulnerability is the most important emotion that we have as humans.
sentences.zh: 如果你把所有这些推理追溯到它的源头，她实际上是在说，脆弱是我们作为人类所拥有的最重要的情感。

sentences.en: Now, the reason so many of us feel so alone, especially in this generation, especially in our 20s, she argues that it's because really what we're struggling to do
sentences.zh: 现在，我们当中有这么多人感到如此孤独的原因，尤其是在我们这一代人当中，特别是在我们二十多岁的时候，她认为这实际上是因为我们真正挣扎着去做的事情是

sentences.en: is let others see us deeply.
sentences.zh: 让别人深入地了解我们。

sentences.en: And we're very afraid that once they peek behind this curtain that we're kind of keeping up, soon they may see things that they didn't want to see
sentences.zh: 我们非常害怕一旦他们偷窥到我们一直高高挂起的这层窗帘后面，他们很快就会看到一些他们不想看到的东西，

sentences.en: and that we didn't want them to see.
sentences.zh: 也是我们不想让他们看到的东西。

sentences.en: And they will find a reason not to love us.
sentences.zh: 并且他们会找到一个不爱我们的理由。

sentences.en: And so any kind of vulnerability, you know, risks that kind of exposure.
sentences.zh: 因此，任何形式的敞开心扉，你知道的，都伴随着这种被看穿的风险。

sentences.en: So we avoid it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们选择逃避。

sentences.en: We keep our walls up, even though we do truly want to be known and we want to be seen by other people.
sentences.zh: 我们高筑心墙，尽管我们内心深处确实渴望被他人了解、被他人看见。

sentences.en: Part of our aversion to vulnerability includes the experience of a vulnerability hangover, this feeling of regret, anxiety, shame that follows sharing something really personal
sentences.zh: 我们对敞开心扉的抗拒感，还包括经历情绪宿醉的体验——这种在与他人（无论是刻意还是无意）分享了非常私密的事情之后，随之而来的后悔、焦虑和羞耻感。

sentences.en: with someone else, either intentionally or accidentally.
sentences.zh: 所以这正是情绪宿醉所带来的真实感受。

sentences.en: So this is exactly what a vulnerability hangover can feel like.
sentences.zh: 你可能会发现自己对说过的一言一行都在进行马后炮式的反复琢磨，

sentences.en: You may find yourself second-guessing every single thing you've said,
sentences.zh: 陷入反刍思维，思考当时本可以有不同的说法，同时还努力回忆另一个人当时确切的表情、他们说了什么、你说了什么，

sentences.en: ruminating, thinking about what you could have said differently, but also trying to remember exactly how the other person looked, what they said, what you said,
sentences.zh: 以及他们对某些信息或话语的具体反应。

sentences.en: what their exact reaction was to certain pieces of information or words.
sentences.zh: 这就像是对当时情境的一种事后情感监控，本意是想让自己感觉好受一点、进行自我抚慰，

sentences.en: It's this kind of posthumous, like emotional monitoring of the situation with the intention of almost trying to make yourself feel better and self-soothe,
sentences.zh: 但实际上却是在伤口上再次撒盐。

sentences.en: but actually picking further at the wound.
sentences.zh: 你可能还会经历羞耻感的恶性循环。

sentences.en: You may also experience shame spirals.
sentences.zh: 我为什么要那样说？

sentences.en: Why did I say that?
sentences.zh: 我为什么要那样做？

sentences.en: Why did I do that?
sentences.zh: 我真是一个糟糕的人。

sentences.en: I'm a bad person.
sentences.zh: 我不配和别人相处。

sentences.en: I don't deserve to be around people.
sentences.zh: 比如，我不配拥有这些情感。

sentences.en: Like, I don't deserve to have these emotions.
sentences.zh: 羞耻、羞耻、羞耻，把你拉入一个极其低谷的情绪状态。

sentences.en: Shame, shame, shame, getting you to a very low point.
sentences.zh: 事后会突然产生一种想要退缩的渴望，

sentences.en: There's this sudden desire to withdraw
sentences.zh: 或者下意识地回避这个人，因为害怕他们对你的态度现在可能会发生改变，而这会彻底证实你的确踩错了步子、

sentences.en: or an avoidance of this person afterwards out of fear that maybe their behavior towards you will now be different and that will confirm once and for all that you did misstep
sentences.zh: 说错了话。

sentences.en: and say the wrong thing.
sentences.zh: 你会产生一种想要去修补、去淡化你所分享的内容、甚至想要出尔反尔的冲动，同时还伴随着真实的身体不适感。

sentences.en: There's the urge to fix it, to downplay what you shared, to kind of go back on your word and also a real physical discomfort.
sentences.zh: 这种感觉就像是夹杂着

sentences.en: It feels like this mixture between
sentences.zh: 焦虑、想要逃跑的冲动，但同时又渴望静静地呆着，希望时间能快点过去，这样你就不用再去想它了。

sentences.en: anxiety, the desire to run away but also the desire to stay still and hope that you know, time will move on and you won't have to think about it.
sentences.zh: 甚至还伴随着恶心感。

sentences.en: There's this nausea.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一种极其复杂、复杂的感觉组合，或者说各种感觉的复杂交织。

sentences.en: It's just this complicated, complicated sensations, complicated combination of sensations I should say.
sentences.zh: 我听过对此最好的描述，

sentences.en: The best way
sentences.zh: 其实就是无意中因为分享过度而让自己感到一阵恶心，而这真的就是它的本质，对吧？

sentences.en: I've actually heard it described is like unconsciously giving yourself the ick from oversharing and really that's exactly what it is, right?
sentences.zh: 不过从一开始就知道这一点至关重要，那就是：并非所有的情绪宿醉都是一样的。

sentences.en: It's really essential to know though, right from the beginning, that not all vulnerability hangovers are created equal.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它们分为两个截然不同的类别。

sentences.en: In fact, there are two distinct categories.
sentences.zh: 第一种情况是，我们其实并不想透露某些事情，但最终还是说出来了。

sentences.en: The first is situations where we didn't really want to reveal something but we did.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，例如在喝了酒之后透露太多，在直觉已经告诉你这是个坏主意的时候向错误的人吐露心声，或者你知道的，

sentences.en: You know, for example, disclosing too much when you've been drinking, confiding in the wrong person when your instincts were already telling you it was a bad idea or, you know,
sentences.zh: 只是不小心说漏了嘴，而你根本没有完全准备好去深入探讨这个话题。

sentences.en: just accidentally letting something slip, you really weren't fully prepared to go in depth on.
sentences.zh: 第二种情况发生在我们确实觉得有必要保持诚实和坦诚，但在事后我们依然感到非常不舒服，尽管我们当时知道、

sentences.en: The second situation occurs when we did feel like it was necessary to be honest and open but we still feel really uncomfortable after the fact even though we knew and we
